title: Prophecy Against Egypt

questions.question: Against whom does Ezekiel prophesy in the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day of the month?
options: Pharaoh king of Egypt, and against all Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh king of Egypt, and against all Egypt
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:2 (ESV): "Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt;"

questions.question: God calls Pharaoh king of Egypt a "great dragon" that lies in the midst of his streams. What prideful statement did Pharaoh make?
options: "My Nile is my own; I made it for myself."
"I will rule the earth and the heavens above it."
"Babylon is but a speck of dust next to my pyramids."
questions.correctAnswer: "My Nile is my own; I made it for myself."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:3 (ESV): "...the great dragon that lies in the midst of his streams, that says, 'My Nile is my own; I made it for myself.'"

questions.question: What does God say He will put in Pharaoh's jaws?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:4 (ESV): "I will put hooks in your jaws, and make the fish of your streams stick to your scales..."

questions.question: Where will God cast Pharaoh and the fish of his streams (his army)?
options: Into the wilderness, onto the open field, to be food for the beasts and birds
Into the boiling pot of Babylon
Into the deep sea where no man goes
questions.correctAnswer: Into the wilderness, onto the open field, to be food for the beasts and birds
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:5 (ESV): "And I will cast you out into the wilderness, you and all the fish of your streams; you shall fall on the open field... I have given you as food to the beasts of the earth and to the birds of the heavens."

questions.question: What object does God compare Egypt to, describing their failure to help the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:6 (ESV): "Then all the inhabitants of Egypt shall know that I am the Lord. Because you have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel,"

questions.question: What happened to Israel when they grasped the staff of Egypt by the hand?
options: You broke and tore all their shoulders
You stood firm for a moment then cracked
questions.correctAnswer: You broke and tore all their shoulders
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:7 (ESV): "when they grasped you with the hand, you broke and tore all their shoulders; and when they leaned on you, you broke and made all their loins to shake."

questions.question: For how many years will God make the land of Egypt an utter waste and desolation?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:11 (ESV): "No foot of man shall pass through it, and no foot of beast shall pass through it; it shall be uninhabited forty years."

questions.question: During those forty years, what will happen to the Egyptians?
options: God will scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries
They will be slaves building the walls of Babylon
They will wander the desert like the Israelites did
They will all be smitten with plagues
questions.correctAnswer: God will scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:12 (ESV): "I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and disperse them through the countries."

questions.question: What will God do at the end of the forty years?
options: Gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered, and restore their fortunes
Send fire from heaven to consume the remnant
Give them a new Pharaoh chosen from Judah
Fill the Nile with blood again
questions.correctAnswer: Gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered, and restore their fortunes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:13-14 (ESV): "For thus says the Lord God: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered, and I will restore the fortunes of Egypt..."

questions.question: When Egypt is restored to the land of Pathros (their origin), what kind of kingdom shall they be?
options: A lowly kingdom; it shall be the most lowly of kingdoms, and never again exalt itself above the nations
A holy nation serving the Lord wholeheartedly
A nation of priests to the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: A lowly kingdom; it shall be the most lowly of kingdoms, and never again exalt itself above the nations
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:14-15 (ESV): "and there they shall be a lowly kingdom. It shall be the most lowly of the kingdoms, and never again exalt itself above the nations."

questions.question: When Egypt becomes a lowly kingdom, she will never again be what to the house of Israel?
options: The reliance of the house of Israel, recalling their iniquity
A place of refuge during famine
questions.correctAnswer: The reliance of the house of Israel, recalling their iniquity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:16 (ESV): "And it shall never again be the reliance of the house of Israel, recalling their iniquity, when they turn to them for aid."

questions.question: In the twenty-seventh year of Ezekiel's exile, God speaks again about Egypt. Who does He say labored hard against Tyre but got no reward?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:18 (ESV): "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labor hard against Tyre... yet neither he nor his army got anything from Tyre to pay for the labor that he had performed against her."

questions.question: Because Nebuchadnezzar worked hard against Tyre (carrying out God's judgment, though unrewarded by Tyre's wealth), what will God give him as his wages?
options: The treasures of the temple in Jerusalem
A long life and a peaceful death
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:19-20 (ESV): "Behold, I will give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and he shall carry off its wealth... I have given him the land of Egypt as his payment for which he labored, because they worked for me..."

questions.question: On that day (when Egypt is destroyed), what will God cause to sprout for the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:21 (ESV): "On that day I will cause a horn to sprout for the house of Israel, and I will open your lips among them. Then they will know that I am the Lord."

questions.question: According to verse 9, what was the prideful reason the land of Egypt shall be a desolation and a waste?
options: Because you said, "The Nile is mine, and I made it"
Because they trusted in their horses and chariots
Because they killed the prophets of God
Because they sought an alliance with Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Because you said, "The Nile is mine, and I made it"
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 29:9 (ESV): "and the land of Egypt shall be a desolation and a waste. Then they will know that I am the Lord. Because you said, 'The Nile is mine, and I made it,'"

key_verse_text: "speak, and say, Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his streams, that says, 'My Nile is my own; I made it for myself.'"
